icp: Jaime Henriques and the Helix specialist-agent fleet
pain: The existing Hermes Desktop build cannot expose durable profiles as specialized Bots or coordinate them in group chats without losing two Helix runtime fixes.
revenueHypothesis: A durable multi-Bot operating surface lowers model and coordination cost and accelerates verified delivery across Finsyt, Cardr, and other Helix revenue products.
mvpAcceptance: Official Bot Mode source and UI tests pass at the pinned upstream commit plus the two preserved Helix regression fixes.
The installed macOS app exposes the existing profile roster as named Bots with independent role, model, memory, skills, avatar metadata, and history.
A bounded three-Bot group chat demonstrates bot-to-bot mention routing and survives an app restart.
Existing profile histories remain readable and the encrypted rollback bundle verifies.
rollback: Restore the pre-Bot-Mode Git branch and app bundle; mount the AES-256 rollback image with its secret-store key and restore profile databases or metadata only if readback proves corruption.
stopConditions: Stop on secret exposure, profile loss, database corruption, target ambiguity, more than three failed implementation attempts, or failure of Bot Mode/history-persistence acceptance.

vercel.exceptionReason: Hermes Desktop and its local Python runtime execute as a native macOS agent and cannot be hosted on Vercel.
